item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — The a16z Show: Fei Fei Li: The Race to Build World Models For AI
item.content:encoded:
Score: 82/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 04 Sep 2026

The episode features a highly authoritative guest discussing cutting-edge AI research (world models) with direct implications for product strategy in AI, robotics, and creative industries. The focus on 'new view prediction' and the challenges of real-world data are strategically relevant for a Senior PM.

Summary

This episode features Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, and Ben Mildenhall, co-founders of World Labs, discussing their new world model, Atlas, with a16z General Partner Martin Casado. The core innovation of Atlas is 'new view prediction,' which integrates generation and 3D reconstruction by predicting how an environment would look from different spatial and temporal perspectives. The conversation delves into the technical underpinnings of Atlas, its current capabilities and limitations, and the critical role of dynamics, editability, and simulation in the evolution of world models. They also explore potential applications in creative fields, architecture, and robotics, highlighting the significant challenge of acquiring sufficient real-world training data for these advanced AI systems.

Key Ideas

  • The 'new view prediction' primitive, central to Atlas, unifies 3D reconstruction and generation, suggesting a potential foundational shift in how AI models understand and interact with the physical world, moving beyond static scene understanding.
  • A primary constraint for the advancement of world models and their applications in robotics and creative work is the scarcity of real-world training data, indicating a strategic bottleneck for product development in these areas.
  • The development of world models necessitates a focus on dynamics, editability, and simulation, implying that future AI product strategies must account for these capabilities to build truly intelligent and adaptable systems.

Implications

For a Senior PM, this episode highlights the strategic importance of investing in AI research that bridges perception and generation, particularly in 3D and spatial intelligence. It underscores the need to consider data acquisition strategies for real-world environments as a critical enabler for advanced AI products in robotics, design, and simulation. The discussion on dynamics and editability suggests that product roadmaps for AI should increasingly incorporate features that allow for interactive and adaptable model outputs, moving beyond static predictions.

item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #2 — Masters of Scale: When AI agents do your shopping, everything changes, with Shopify’s Jess Hertz
item.ns1:encoded:
Score: 84/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 01 Sep 2026

The episode directly addresses the strategic implications of AI agents in eCommerce, a core focus area, with a high-authority guest from Shopify. The insights on discoverability and infrastructure for AI-driven shopping are highly relevant for a Senior PM.

Summary

This episode explores how AI agents are transforming the eCommerce landscape, moving beyond traditional search result dominance by large brands. Shopify COO Jess Hertz discusses the company's data insights into this agentic shopping revolution and how Shopify is building the necessary infrastructure for AI-driven product discovery and purchase. The conversation also touches on Shopify's approach to AI token spending and its strategic commitment to leading in this new era of online shopping, given its significant market share.

Key Ideas

  • AI agents are shifting eCommerce power from brands that can buy top search results to those optimized for AI-driven discoverability and purchase, requiring a fundamental change in product strategy.
  • Shopify's internal policy allows engineers to spend freely on AI tokens, indicating a strategic prioritization of AI development over immediate ROI concerns, suggesting a 'win the future or die trying' approach.
  • The emergence of AI agents necessitates new infrastructure layers for products to be discoverable and purchasable by AI, implying a significant platform-level shift for eCommerce providers.

Implications

Senior PMs in eCommerce need to re-evaluate product discoverability strategies, invest in AI-compatible infrastructure, and understand the shift from human-centric search to agent-centric purchasing. This also suggests a need to explore new business models and partnerships within the AI agent ecosystem.
